summary: Response usage preserves actual model/provider/API, response identity, reasoning and cache-TTL subsets, timestamps, duration and TTFT. OMP object-shaped USD costs retain their total and components through the existing accounting path; premium requests remain separately typed provider quota, never tokens or money.

replay.detail: No replay or historical backfill. Previously captured observations keep their original fields and omissions. Repeated terminal channel snapshots use provider response IDs when available.

schema.detail: TimelineUsageBody gains optional provider, account, response_id, api, stop_reason, started_at_unix_ms, completed_at_unix_ms, duration_ms, ttft_ms, cache_write_1h_tokens, reasoning_tokens, cost_components and provider_quota. Response total_tokens is optional when unobserved; session cumulative totals remain required. Rust and Swift model templates expose the same fields; TypeScript models and codecs derive from the schema.

rules.detail: No claim, retention, invocation-attribution or accounting authority change. Reported scalar total still wins over shared price-table estimates. Metadata-only responses create no spend receipt; incomplete token buckets or unknown nonzero-write TTL remain unpriced rather than zero-filled for estimates. Cost components and token subsets are not additive spend.

compatibility.detail: Older observations decode with unknown optional evidence. Numeric scalar channel cost remains supported alongside OMP object-shaped cost. Missing unsupported counters and actual model observations are no longer manufactured as zeros or copied from launch requests. Older strict schema validators must update to accept the additional optional response fields.

downtime.detail: Ordinary rolling deployment; no database conversion or additional startup work.

recovery.detail: No new recovery path, ledger or rate card. Unsupported or absent evidence remains unknown rather than being reconstructed.
